explanation: A strike knocks down all ten pins with the first ball of a frame, and a spare clears the rest with the second. Twelve strikes in a row make a perfect game of 300.

claims.text: Strikes and spares are scoring terms in ten-pin bowling.
Spares are not part of scoring in baseball, darts or curling; baseball has strikes but no spares.
In ten-pin bowling a strike is knocking down all ten pins with the first ball of a frame, and a spare is knocking down the remaining pins with the second ball.
A perfect game in ten-pin bowling is 12 strikes in a row, for a score of 300.

claimResults.note: Answered cold. The pairing 'strikes and spares' is unique to bowling games among the options.

evidence.restatement: No spare exists in curling, darts or baseball; baseball counts strikes against a batter but has nothing called a spare.

claimResults.note: Baseball is the tempting distractor because of 'strikes', but only bowling has both terms, so the stem's pair rules it out. Curling (ends, stones) and darts (legs, sets) have neither.

evidence.restatement: A strike means all ten pins fall to the first delivery in a frame; a spare means the second delivery topples whatever pins the first left standing.

claimResults.note: Standard bowling definitions (World Bowling / USBC rules).

evidence.restatement: The maximum ten-pin score is 300, reached by bowling strikes on all twelve possible deliveries: one in each of frames 1 to 9 and three in the tenth.

claimResults.note: Each strike frame scores 10 plus the next two balls; ten frames of 30 make 300, needing 9 + 3 = 12 consecutive strikes.

evidence.restatement: Ten-pin bowling scores are built from strikes and spares.

claimResults.note: Rival test: baseball strikes are counts against a batter, not scoring; darts and curling use neither term.

evidence.restatement: Only bowling has spares; baseball has strikes but no spares, and darts and curling have neither.
Knocking all ten pins down with the first ball is a strike; clearing what is left with the second ball is a spare.
Twelve straight strikes give the maximum score of 300 in ten-pin bowling.

claimResults.note: Ten frames plus two bonus balls make twelve strikes, and each frame is worth 30, so 10 x 30 = 300.
